query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Using a machine-learning-based potential (MLP) trained on ab initio molecular dynamics simulations can improve the representation of high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states near their high melting temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states
generation.intervention: Machine-learning-based potential (MLP) training on ab initio molecular dynamics simulations
generation.conditions: Temperatures near the high melting points of the alloys, applicable composition ranges include equiatomic and non-equiatomic multicomponent alloys
generation.mechanism: Enhanced phase-space overlap between the reference and target systems due to the MLP's ability to capture complex many-body interactions
generation.predicted_outcome: Reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least 30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references, as measured by the free-energy difference between the solid and liquid phases
generation.boundary: Composition ranges: 3-6 principal elements, Temperature ranges: 0.8-1.2 T_m, where T_m is the melting temperature
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the MLP may depend on the quality and quantity of the training data, as well as the specific alloy composition and temperature range

falsification_experiment.design: Free-energy calculation using thermodynamic integration with the MLP and EAM references
measurements: Free-energy difference between solid and liquid phases
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the MLP does not reduce the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least 20% relative to the EAM references, the hypothesis is falsified
